newsitem.title: USA: Sweden to probe its wartime past, Jewish group says.
newsitem.headline: Sweden to probe its wartime past, Jewish group says.

text.p: Sweden has agreed to launch a full-scale probe into its wartime dealings with the Nazis, including setting up an official commission of inquiry, the World Jewish Congress said on Tuesday.
The WJC said the agreement was reached at a meeting between its secretary general Israel Singer and Swedish Prime Minster Goran Persson earlier in the day in Stockholm.

WJC Executive Director Elan Steinberg said Sweden promised a comprehensive examination of its handling of bank accounts of Jewish victims of the Holocaust and its trade with the Nazis during the war. Sweden was one of four neutral nations in Europe whose dealings with the Third Reich have come under scrutiny as part of a two-year probe into Swiss dealings with the Nazis.

Previously secret U.S. government documents allege that Switzerland received hundreds of millions of dollars in gold looted by the Nazis from the countries they conquered in exchange for currency to buy vitally needed war materials.

The WJC said some 900 dormant accounts believed to have belonged to Jews who perished in the Holocaust have been discovered in Swedish banks. A commission of historians and government officials has been established in Sweden to investigate and is expected to report back in a year, it said.
Documents found in the U.S. National Archives show that the Germans shipped 23 tons of looted gold to Sweden primarily to buy iron ore.

WJC Vice President Kalman Sultanik said, "We have agreed to turn over to Sweden thousands of documents we have uncovered to help their research. The willingness of Sweden to confront its past is a model for other nations to follow."
